records.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town

He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. records.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
records.bio: G. J. Utterson is a lawyer, a kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and an old friend of both Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past who is troubled by old sins. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

records.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
records.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

records.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
records.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

records.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
records.bio: Poole is the elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house, obedient to his master and to Hyde as his superior. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. Utterson now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering, and Poole reports that Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

records.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
records.bio: Gabriel John Utterson is a lawyer, the distant kinsman of Richard Enfield, and the friend and legal adviser of Dr. Jekyll. He is a man of steady habits, uneasy and concerned for Jekyll, and known as the last good influence on downgoing men. He introduced Enfield to Jekyll and long handled Jekyll's affairs, including a will naming Hyde as heir. When Poole came to him at night fearing foul play, Utterson followed him to Jekyll's house, questioned the servants, and resolved to break in. After the cabinet door was burst open, he found Hyde's body and searched for Jekyll. He now holds Jekyll's sealed packet and intends to read the documents and return before midnight to send for the police.

records.tagline: Elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house
records.bio: Poole is the elderly butler of Dr. Jekyll's house and the servant who directs the search after the cabinet is broken open. He is frightened and worn, with a white face and a harsh broken voice, and for about a week he has been unable to bear the situation. He long served Jekyll, admitted Utterson to the cabinet, and reported that Jekyll confined himself over the laboratory. When he came to Utterson's house at night, he said the doctor had shut himself in and he feared foul play. He led Utterson to the laboratory, told of the masked figure, and struck the door with an axe. He now hands Utterson the sealed packet and awaits the police.

records.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
records.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, owner of the house with laboratory and cabinet, and the friend and client of Mr. Utterson. He is tall and well built, known for charities and religion, but has become fanciful and estranged from Dr. Lanyon. His will left all his possessions to Edward Hyde, and he admitted Hyde dictated its terms. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, then resumed his old friendships before shutting his door against Utterson and vowing extreme seclusion. He was last seen sitting sadly at the middle window, declining to walk out. He is said to have been made away with eight days ago, and his body has not been found.

records.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
records.bio: Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town, acquainted with Dr. Jekyll. He dislikes asking questions and calls this delicacy. He once collared a man who walked over a child and forced him to pay a hundred pounds, then spent the night in his chambers and proved the cheque genuine at the bank. He named the man as Hyde and described him as deformed and detestable. He later learned the sinister door was a back way to Jekyll's house. On a Sunday walk with Utterson he said the Hyde story was at an end, and after seeing Jekyll at the window he left the court in silence, pale with horror.

records.tagline: Voice inside the cabinet refusing entry
records.bio: The voice is the unseen speaker inside Dr. Jekyll's cabinet, heard by Poole and Mr. Utterson during the night search. It complains that it cannot see anyone and begs Utterson for mercy. It is connected to Poole only as the servant who knocks and calls through the door. After Poole reports that the doctor has shut himself in, the voice answers from within and refuses entry. Utterson recognizes it as Hyde's voice and orders the door down. The voice is now silent, its speaker found dead inside the cabinet.

records.tagline: Servant who weeps hysterically
records.bio: The housemaid is a servant in Dr. Jekyll's house, subordinate to Poole and a colleague of the cook. She is hysterical and weeping. When Poole led Utterson into the hall, all the servants were huddled in fear, and she whimpered while the maid wept loudly. She remains in the hall with the other frightened servants as Utterson and Poole proceed to the laboratory. Her present situation is one of terror and grief among the household while the search for Jekyll continues.

records.text:
During a Sunday walk, Utterson and Enfield stop at a sinister door. Enfield recalls Hyde trampling a girl, then paying her family £100 with a genuine cheque. Utterson studies Jekyll’s will, which leaves everything to Hyde if Jekyll vanishes. Lanyon says Jekyll grew too fanciful and has never heard of Hyde. Keeping watch, Utterson accosts Hyde, who admits Jekyll is out, gives a Soho address, then snarls and disappears inside. Poole confirms Hyde has a key and all servants must obey him. Jekyll pales when Utterson mentions Hyde, refuses more, but says he can be rid of Hyde whenever he chooses. He asks Utterson to help Hyde for his sake when gone.

A maid saw Hyde cane Sir Danvers Carew to death. The mangled body bore a sealed envelope for Utterson, who identified Carew. Inspector Newcomen showed the broken stick, which Utterson recognized as Jekyll’s gift. They searched Hyde’s rooms, finding the other half and a burnt cheque book. Hyde had thousands at the bank, but few familiars, no photograph, and wildly differing descriptions.

Poole admits Utterson to Jekyll’s cabinet. Jekyll swears he will never see Hyde again. Jekyll gives Utterson a letter signed Edward Hyde, saying he burned the envelope, which had no postmark, and that Hyde dictated his will. Poole says no letter came except by post. Guest finds the murderer’s letter identical to Jekyll’s note. Utterson locks it in his safe, suspecting forgery.

After the murder, Hyde vanishes and rewards are offered. Jekyll resumes old friendships, then shuts his door; Poole says he is confined. Utterson finds Lanyon decayed, doomed, refusing Jekyll’s name. Lanyon dies within a fortnight. After the funeral, Utterson opens Lanyon’s sealed envelope, not to be opened till Jekyll’s death or disappearance. Poole reports Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory, silent.

On another Sunday walk, Utterson and Enfield stop at the by-street door. Enfield says the Hyde affair is over, but Utterson admits he once saw Hyde and felt the same repulsion. Enfield reveals the door is Jekyll’s back way. Looking up, Utterson sees Jekyll sadly at the middle window. Jekyll says he is very low and it will not last long. He declines their walk, saying he dare not. When Utterson suggests talking from below, Jekyll’s smile becomes abject terror and the window is thrust down. The two men leave the court in silence, pale with horror, Utterson saying “God forgive us” twice.

Poole comes to Utterson at night, fearing foul play. They walk to Jekyll’s house, where servants huddle terrified. Poole leads Utterson to the cabinet; a changed voice refuses them. Poole claims Jekyll was murdered eight days ago and saw a masked dwarf—Mr. Hyde. Utterson resolves to break in. Poole strikes the door five times with an axe. Inside lies Hyde’s contorted body, a crushed phial nearby. They search for Jekyll but find only chemicals, a blasphemous book, a will naming Utterson, and a sealed packet. Utterson plans to read the documents and return before midnight.

records.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor.
records.bio: Hastie Lanyon is a doctor and colleague of Henry Jekyll, and an old friend of Mr. Utterson. He is cautious and suspicious of Jekyll's sanity. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind, and later refused to hear Jekyll's name, calling him dead to him. After dining with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, he was shocked by his own decayed appearance and declared himself a doomed man who would never recover. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened his sealed envelope.

records.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir.
records.bio: Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, colleague of Dr. Lanyon, and lawyer Utterson's acquaintance, known for charities and religion. He is hunted across the land as Carew's murderer. He swore never to set eyes on Hyde again, admitted Hyde dictated his will, and after Hyde vanished resumed his old friendships. He then shut his door against Utterson, vowed extreme seclusion, and spoke of an unnameable punishment. On the ninth of January he begged Lanyon to force open his cabinet, take the fourth drawer, and receive a midnight messenger. Lanyon obeyed, and Jekyll confessed his moral turpitude with tears.

records.tagline: Small man who comes at midnight in Jekyll's name.
records.bio: The small man is a secret midnight visitor who comes in Dr. Jekyll's name to Dr. Lanyon's house. He is small, with a shocking facial expression. At midnight he knocked gently and crouched against the portico pillars; when Lanyon asked if he came from Dr. Jekyll, he gestured yes. He glanced back at a policeman and hurried inside. Lanyon then saw him clearly for the first time and was struck by his appearance. He is currently at Lanyon's house, having come secretly at midnight in Jekyll's name.

records.tagline: Elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house.
records.bio: Poole is the elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, obeyed by the housemaid, cook, and knife-boy, and directed by Mr. Utterson in the search. He is afraid and cannot bear it, with a white face and harsh broken voice. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, that Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, and that all servants had orders to obey Hyde. Later he reported Jekyll confined and silent, came to Utterson at night, and said he thought there had been foul play. He and Utterson broke in and found Hyde's body. He currently awaits Lanyon's arrival with a locksmith.

Lanyon welcomed him warmly, said Jekyll had become too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago, and had never heard of Hyde. He confirmed that Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door, that all servants have orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory. Utterson asked Lanyon whether they were Jekyll's two oldest friends. Jekyll is now from home, gone out, while his servants are ordered to obey Hyde.

$tuple.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
$tuple.bio: Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, connoisseur, and friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. After dinner with Utterson, Jekyll refused to hear more of Hyde, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

$tuple.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
$tuple.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

$tuple.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
$tuple.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

$tuple.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
$tuple.bio: Poole is the elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house, obedient to his master and to Hyde as his superior. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. Utterson now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering, and Poole reports that Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

$tuple.tagline: Utterson's head clerk and handwriting expert

$tuple.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
$tuple.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

$tuple.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
$tuple.bio: Gabriel John Utterson is a lawyer, the distant kinsman of Richard Enfield, and the friend and legal adviser of Dr. Jekyll. He is a man of steady habits, uneasy and concerned for Jekyll, and known as the last good influence on downgoing men. He introduced Enfield to Jekyll and long handled Jekyll's affairs, including a will naming Hyde as heir. When Poole came to him at night fearing foul play, Utterson followed him to Jekyll's house, questioned the servants, and resolved to break in. After the cabinet door was burst open, he found Hyde's body and searched for Jekyll. He now holds Jekyll's sealed packet and intends to read the documents and return before midnight to send for the police.

$tuple.tagline: Elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house
$tuple.bio: Poole is the elderly butler of Dr. Jekyll's house and the servant who directs the search after the cabinet is broken open. He is frightened and worn, with a white face and a harsh broken voice, and for about a week he has been unable to bear the situation. He long served Jekyll, admitted Utterson to the cabinet, and reported that Jekyll confined himself over the laboratory. When he came to Utterson's house at night, he said the doctor had shut himself in and he feared foul play. He led Utterson to the laboratory, told of the masked figure, and struck the door with an axe. He now hands Utterson the sealed packet and awaits the police.

$tuple.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
$tuple.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, owner of the house with laboratory and cabinet, and the friend and client of Mr. Utterson. He is tall and well built, known for charities and religion, but has become fanciful and estranged from Dr. Lanyon. His will left all his possessions to Edward Hyde, and he admitted Hyde dictated its terms. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, then resumed his old friendships before shutting his door against Utterson and vowing extreme seclusion. He was last seen sitting sadly at the middle window, declining to walk out. He is said to have been made away with eight days ago, and his body has not been found.

$tuple.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
$tuple.bio: Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town, acquainted with Dr. Jekyll. He dislikes asking questions and calls this delicacy. He once collared a man who walked over a child and forced him to pay a hundred pounds, then spent the night in his chambers and proved the cheque genuine at the bank. He named the man as Hyde and described him as deformed and detestable. He later learned the sinister door was a back way to Jekyll's house. On a Sunday walk with Utterson he said the Hyde story was at an end, and after seeing Jekyll at the window he left the court in silence, pale with horror.

$tuple.tagline: Voice inside the cabinet refusing entry
$tuple.bio: The voice is the unseen speaker inside Dr. Jekyll's cabinet, heard by Poole and Mr. Utterson during the night search. It complains that it cannot see anyone and begs Utterson for mercy. It is connected to Poole only as the servant who knocks and calls through the door. After Poole reports that the doctor has shut himself in, the voice answers from within and refuses entry. Utterson recognizes it as Hyde's voice and orders the door down. The voice is now silent, its speaker found dead inside the cabinet.

$tuple.tagline: Servant who weeps hysterically
$tuple.bio: The housemaid is a servant in Dr. Jekyll's house, subordinate to Poole and a colleague of the cook. She is hysterical and weeping. When Poole led Utterson into the hall, all the servants were huddled in fear, and she whimpered while the maid wept loudly. She remains in the hall with the other frightened servants as Utterson and Poole proceed to the laboratory. Her present situation is one of terror and grief among the household while the search for Jekyll continues.

Lanyon dies within a fortnight. After the funeral, Utterson opens Lanyon’s sealed envelope, not to be opened till Jekyll’s death or disappearance. Poole reports Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory, silent.

On another Sunday walk, Utterson and Enfield stop at the by-street door. Enfield says the Hyde affair is over, but Utterson admits he once saw Hyde and felt the same repulsion. Enfield reveals the door is Jekyll’s back way. Looking up, Utterson sees Jekyll sadly at the middle window. Jekyll says he is very low and it will not last long. He declines their walk, saying he dare not. When Utterson suggests talking from below, Jekyll’s smile becomes abject terror and the window is thrust down. The two men leave the court in silence, pale with horror, Utterson saying “God forgive us” twice.

Poole comes to Utterson at night, fearing foul play. They walk to Jekyll’s house, where servants huddle terrified. Poole leads Utterson to the cabinet; a changed voice refuses them. Poole claims Jekyll was murdered eight days ago and saw a masked dwarf—Mr. Hyde. Utterson resolves to break in. Poole strikes the door five times with an axe. Inside lies Hyde’s contorted body, a crushed phial nearby. They search for Jekyll but find only chemicals, a blasphemous book, a will naming Utterson, and a sealed packet. Utterson plans to read the documents and return before midnight.

$tuple.text: Dr. Lanyon receives a desperate letter from Henry Jekyll, who begs him to break into his cabinet, take the fourth drawer, and hand it to a midnight messenger. Lanyon obeys, waits armed, and admits a small, crouching man who claims to come from Jekyll. $tuple.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor.
$tuple.bio: Hastie Lanyon is a doctor and colleague of Henry Jekyll, and an old friend of Mr. Utterson. He is cautious and suspicious of Jekyll's sanity. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind, and later refused to hear Jekyll's name, calling him dead to him. After dining with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, he was shocked by his own decayed appearance and declared himself a doomed man who would never recover. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened his sealed envelope.

$tuple.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir.
$tuple.bio: Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, colleague of Dr. Lanyon, and lawyer Utterson's acquaintance, known for charities and religion. He is hunted across the land as Carew's murderer. He swore never to set eyes on Hyde again, admitted Hyde dictated his will, and after Hyde vanished resumed his old friendships. He then shut his door against Utterson, vowed extreme seclusion, and spoke of an unnameable punishment. On the ninth of January he begged Lanyon to force open his cabinet, take the fourth drawer, and receive a midnight messenger. Lanyon obeyed, and Jekyll confessed his moral turpitude with tears.

$tuple.tagline: Small man who comes at midnight in Jekyll's name.
$tuple.bio: The small man is a secret midnight visitor who comes in Dr. Jekyll's name to Dr. Lanyon's house. He is small, with a shocking facial expression. At midnight he knocked gently and crouched against the portico pillars; when Lanyon asked if he came from Dr. Jekyll, he gestured yes. He glanced back at a policeman and hurried inside. Lanyon then saw him clearly for the first time and was struck by his appearance. He is currently at Lanyon's house, having come secretly at midnight in Jekyll's name.

$tuple.tagline: Elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house.
$tuple.bio: Poole is the elderly butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, obeyed by the housemaid, cook, and knife-boy, and directed by Mr. Utterson in the search. He is afraid and cannot bear it, with a white face and harsh broken voice. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, that Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, and that all servants had orders to obey Hyde. Later he reported Jekyll confined and silent, came to Utterson at night, and said he thought there had been foul play. He and Utterson broke in and found Hyde's body. He currently awaits Lanyon's arrival with a locksmith.

records.text: 阿Q回土谷祠后省悟古怪在于自己赤膊，未庄女人见他便躲，邹七嫂也叫女儿进去。酒店不再赊欠，管祠老头子催他走。多日无人叫工，他饿着打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗。阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，相持半点钟后同时放手退开。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，决计出门求食，翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，小尼姑探头又缩回，老尼姑出来斥他偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑，被黑狗追咬，爬上桑树滚出墙外。吃完三个萝卜，他打定进城的主意。

records.tagline: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
records.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

records.tagline: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
records.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

records.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
records.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

records.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
records.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

records.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
records.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

records.tagline: 又癞又胡的未庄人，扭打阿Q使其受辱
records.bio: 未庄人，又癞又胡，人称王癞胡。他与阿Q本无深交，却因捉虱子一事结怨。阿Q与他并排坐下捉虱子，阿Q捉的虱子不如他多，心中不平，骂他毛虫，他回骂癞皮狗，并抓住阿Q辫子撞墙五下，使阿Q受生平第一件屈辱。目前他仍在未庄。

records.tagline: 进秀才的赵家子，被问及阿Q名字
records.bio: 赵太爷之子，进过秀才，人称茂才先生。他出身赵家，对阿Q一类人物并不放在眼里。叙述者曾问他阿Q名字的写法，他茫然不知。阿Q在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉时，他拿大竹杠打阿Q，骂他忘八蛋。目前他仍是赵家的秀才。

records.tagline: 未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人
records.bio: 未庄的闲人们，常以戏弄阿Q为乐。他们拿阿Q的癞疮疤取笑，喊“亮起来了”；揪住阿Q的黄辫子碰响头后得胜而去；又逼阿Q自认人打畜生，阿Q自认虫豸。目前他们仍是未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人。

records.tagline: 赵太爷家唯一女仆，被阿Q调戏
records.bio: 赵太爷家唯一的女仆，是个小孤孀，与邻居邹七嫂相熟。她本分守己，却因阿Q的举动受惊。阿Q在赵家厨房向她下跪求困觉，她楞了一息，发抖大叫着往外跑；少奶奶拖她出下房，邹七嫂劝她不要寻短见。目前她仍在赵太爷家做女仆。

records.tagline: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，抢了阿Q的活
records.bio: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，人称小Don。他本是无名之辈，却因谋了阿Q的饭碗而与阿Q结仇。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗；阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。目前他仍在未庄做短工。

$tuple.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

$tuple.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
$tuple.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

$tuple.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
$tuple.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

$tuple.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
$tuple.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

$tuple.tagline: 又癞又胡的未庄人，扭打阿Q使其受辱
$tuple.bio: 未庄人，又癞又胡，人称王癞胡。他与阿Q本无深交，却因捉虱子一事结怨。阿Q与他并排坐下捉虱子，阿Q捉的虱子不如他多，心中不平，骂他毛虫，他回骂癞皮狗，并抓住阿Q辫子撞墙五下，使阿Q受生平第一件屈辱。目前他仍在未庄。

$tuple.tagline: 进秀才的赵家子，被问及阿Q名字
$tuple.bio: 赵太爷之子，进过秀才，人称茂才先生。他出身赵家，对阿Q一类人物并不放在眼里。叙述者曾问他阿Q名字的写法，他茫然不知。阿Q在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉时，他拿大竹杠打阿Q，骂他忘八蛋。目前他仍是赵家的秀才。

$tuple.tagline: 未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人
$tuple.bio: 未庄的闲人们，常以戏弄阿Q为乐。他们拿阿Q的癞疮疤取笑，喊“亮起来了”；揪住阿Q的黄辫子碰响头后得胜而去；又逼阿Q自认人打畜生，阿Q自认虫豸。目前他们仍是未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人。

$tuple.tagline: 赵太爷家唯一女仆，被阿Q调戏
$tuple.bio: 赵太爷家唯一的女仆，是个小孤孀，与邻居邹七嫂相熟。她本分守己，却因阿Q的举动受惊。阿Q在赵家厨房向她下跪求困觉，她楞了一息，发抖大叫着往外跑；少奶奶拖她出下房，邹七嫂劝她不要寻短见。目前她仍在赵太爷家做女仆。

$tuple.tagline: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，抢了阿Q的活
$tuple.bio: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，人称小Don。他本是无名之辈，却因谋了阿Q的饭碗而与阿Q结仇。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗；阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。目前他仍在未庄做短工。

records.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
records.bio: Mr. Utterson is a lawyer and the distant kinsman and friend of Mr. Richard Enfield. He is austere, tolerant, and undemonstrative, and is known as the last good influence on downgoing men. On a Sunday walk with Enfield, he was shown a sinister door and heard Enfield's account of a man who trampled a girl and paid with a cheque. Utterson asked whether the cheque drawer lived there, asked the man's name, and asked whether Hyde used a key. He said he already knew the other party's name. He and Enfield agreed never to refer to the matter again. He remains a lawyer and the last good influence on downgoing men.

records.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
records.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

records.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
records.bio: The man in the middle, later named Hyde, is a person of extraordinary appearance who gives a feeling of deformity. He is cool, sneering, and Satan-like. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, then was collared by Enfield and brought back to the group around the child. The doctor turned sick and white with desire to kill him. Threatened with scandal, he was forced to pay a hundred pounds. He led them to the door, unlocked it, and returned with gold and a cheque, offering to stay until the banks opened and cash it himself. They spent the night in Enfield's chambers and went to the bank next day. He still has a key and used it a week ago.

records.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
records.bio: Mr. Utterson is a lawyer of Gaunt Street, kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and old friend of Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past, troubled by old sins. Enfield showed him a sinister door and told of a man who trampled a child. Utterson studied Jekyll's will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde. He consulted Lanyon, who had never heard of Hyde. Utterson kept watch by the by-street door until he accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He then learned from Poole that Jekyll was out and that Hyde had a key. He now fears Jekyll is in deep waters.

records.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
records.bio: Edward Hyde is a small, plainly dressed man with a husky, whispering, broken voice, known as Jekyll's friend and benefactor, living in Soho. He is merciless and inspires enduring hatred. He trampled a girl and paid a hundred pounds with a cheque from Jekyll's account. Jekyll's will names him heir if Jekyll vanishes. Utterson accosted him at the by-street door; Hyde gave his Soho address, accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll, then unlocked the door and disappeared. He has a key to Jekyll's house, comes by the dissecting room door, and all servants are ordered to obey him. He now mostly uses the laboratory and never dines there.

records.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
records.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old school and college friend of Mr. Utterson and a friend of Dr. Jekyll. He is hearty, red-faced, prematurely white-haired, boisterous, decided, theatrical but genuine. Utterson came to consult him about Jekyll's will and Hyde. Lanyon welcomed him warmly, said Jekyll had become too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago, and had never heard of Hyde. He now remains Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor, unaware of Hyde's identity.

records.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
records.bio: Poole is the elderly servant and butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, serving his master Dr. Jekyll and obeying the man in the middle as an obeyed superior. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's house and told him Jekyll had gone out. He confirmed that Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door, that all servants have orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory. He now continues in his post, bound by orders to obey Hyde.

records.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
records.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll, M.D., D.C.L., L.L.D., F.R.S., is a doctor, old friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon, and master of Poole. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. Lanyon said Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago. Utterson asked Lanyon whether they were Jekyll's two oldest friends. Jekyll is now from home, gone out, while his servants are ordered to obey Hyde.

$tuple.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
$tuple.bio: Mr. Utterson is a lawyer of Gaunt Street, kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and old friend of Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past, troubled by old sins. Enfield showed him a sinister door and told of a man who trampled a child. Utterson studied Jekyll's will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde. He consulted Lanyon, who had never heard of Hyde. Utterson kept watch by the by-street door until he accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He then learned from Poole that Jekyll was out and that Hyde had a key. He now fears Jekyll is in deep waters.

$tuple.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
$tuple.bio: Edward Hyde is a small, plainly dressed man with a husky, whispering, broken voice, known as Jekyll's friend and benefactor, living in Soho. He is merciless and inspires enduring hatred. He trampled a girl and paid a hundred pounds with a cheque from Jekyll's account. Jekyll's will names him heir if Jekyll vanishes. Utterson accosted him at the by-street door; Hyde gave his Soho address, accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll, then unlocked the door and disappeared. He has a key to Jekyll's house, comes by the dissecting room door, and all servants are ordered to obey him. He now mostly uses the laboratory and never dines there.

$tuple.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
$tuple.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old school and college friend of Mr. Utterson and a friend of Dr. Jekyll. He is hearty, red-faced, prematurely white-haired, boisterous, decided, theatrical but genuine. Utterson came to consult him about Jekyll's will and Hyde. Lanyon welcomed him warmly, said Jekyll had become too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago, and had never heard of Hyde. He now remains Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor, unaware of Hyde's identity.

$tuple.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
$tuple.bio: Poole is the elderly servant and butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, serving his master Dr. Jekyll and obeying the man in the middle as an obeyed superior. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's house and told him Jekyll had gone out. He confirmed that Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door, that all servants have orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory. He now continues in his post, bound by orders to obey Hyde.

$tuple.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
$tuple.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll, M.D., D.C.L., L.L.D., F.R.S., is a doctor, old friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon, and master of Poole. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. Lanyon said Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago. Utterson asked Lanyon whether they were Jekyll's two oldest friends. Jekyll is now from home, gone out, while his servants are ordered to obey Hyde.

During a Sunday walk, Utterson and Enfield stop at a sinister door. Enfield recalls how a man trampled a girl, then paid her family £100 with a cheque that proved genuine. Utterson returns home troubled and studies Jekyll’s will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde if Jekyll vanishes. He calls it madness and fears disgrace. Keeping watch by the by-street door, he accosts a small man with a key, who admits Jekyll is out, gives his Soho address, then snarls and disappears inside. At Jekyll’s house, Poole confirms Hyde has a key, comes by the dissecting room, and all servants must obey him. Utterson goes home fearing Jekyll is in deep waters.

$tuple.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
$tuple.bio: Mr. Utterson is a Gaunt Street lawyer, kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and friend of Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past, troubled by old sins. After Enfield showed him a sinister door and named its user, Utterson studied Jekyll's will, which leaves everything to Edward Hyde. He consulted Lanyon, watched the by-street door, and accosted Hyde. Later he stayed after Jekyll's dinner and promised to help Hyde for Jekyll's sake. He then identified Sir Danvers Carew's body and searched Hyde's rooms. He is now obsessed with finding and seeing Hyde.

$tuple.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
$tuple.bio: Henry Jekyll is a fifty-year-old doctor, connoisseur, and friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon. He is large, well-made, smooth-faced, with a slyish cast, showing capacity and kindness and warm affection for Utterson. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. After dinner with Utterson, Jekyll refused to hear more of Hyde, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He is now painfully situated, his position strange and not mended by talking.

$tuple.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
$tuple.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, living in Soho and served by Poole and an old woman landlady. He is merciless and inspires enduring hatred, impressing beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled a girl and paid a hundred pounds with a cheque. Utterson later accosted him at the by-street door, and Hyde gave his Soho address before disappearing inside. Jekyll called him poor Hyde and asked Utterson to help him. The maid then saw Hyde beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He is now a fugitive with few acquaintances and no traceable family.

$tuple.tagline: Police officer investigating the murder
$tuple.bio: Inspector Newcomen is a Scotland Yard officer investigating the murder of Sir Danvers Carew, working with Mr. Utterson, who guides the investigation. He is a professional police officer. He narrated the maid's account and showed the broken stick. Utterson took him to Hyde's house, where the old woman let them search and they found the other half of the stick and a burnt cheque book. He found several thousand pounds to Hyde's credit at the bank. He now plans to wait for Hyde at the bank and issue handbills.

$tuple.tagline: Murder victim, an aged gentleman
$tuple.bio: Sir Danvers Carew is an aged, beautiful gentleman with white hair, an acquaintance of Mr. Utterson, who later identifies his body. He is an aged gentleman. The maid servant saw Hyde beat him to death with a cane. His body was found mangled in the lane. A sealed envelope addressed to Utterson was found on him. Utterson identified the body as Sir Danvers Carew. He is now dead, murdered by Hyde.

$tuple.tagline: Witness who sees Hyde murder Carew
$tuple.bio: The maid servant is a servant who witnesses the murder of Sir Danvers Carew by Edward Hyde. She is a maid servant. She saw Hyde beat an aged beautiful gentleman with white hair to death with a cane. She fainted at the horror of the murder. She woke at two and called the police. She is now the witness who sees Hyde murder Carew.

records.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

records.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

records.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
records.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

records.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

records.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
records.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

records.tagline: 又癞又胡的未庄人，扭打阿Q使其受辱
records.bio: 未庄人，又癞又胡，人称王癞胡。他与阿Q本无深交，却因捉虱子一事结怨。阿Q与他并排坐下捉虱子，阿Q捉的虱子不如他多，心中不平，骂他毛虫，他回骂癞皮狗，并抓住阿Q辫子撞墙五下，使阿Q受生平第一件屈辱。目前他仍在未庄。

records.tagline: 进秀才的赵家子，被问及阿Q名字
records.bio: 赵太爷之子，进过秀才，人称茂才先生。他出身赵家，对阿Q一类人物并不放在眼里。叙述者曾问他阿Q名字的写法，他茫然不知。阿Q在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉时，他拿大竹杠打阿Q，骂他忘八蛋。目前他仍是赵家的秀才。

records.tagline: 未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人
records.bio: 未庄的闲人们，常以戏弄阿Q为乐。他们拿阿Q的癞疮疤取笑，喊“亮起来了”；揪住阿Q的黄辫子碰响头后得胜而去；又逼阿Q自认人打畜生，阿Q自认虫豸。目前他们仍是未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人。

records.tagline: 赵太爷家唯一女仆，被阿Q调戏
records.bio: 赵太爷家唯一的女仆，是个小孤孀，与邻居邹七嫂相熟。她本分守己，却因阿Q的举动受惊。阿Q在赵家厨房向她下跪求困觉，她楞了一息，发抖大叫着往外跑；少奶奶拖她出下房，邹七嫂劝她不要寻短见。目前她仍在赵太爷家做女仆。

records.tagline: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，抢了阿Q的活
records.bio: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，人称小Don。他本是无名之辈，却因谋了阿Q的饭碗而与阿Q结仇。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗；阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。目前他仍在未庄做短工。

records.value: 腿直了，辫子不见，戴假辫子

records.text: 赵家遭抢四天后，阿Q半夜被兵警抓进县城，关进栅栏小屋。他上大堂见光头老头子，身不由己跪下，供称“因为我想造反”，又答不知同党下落。被令画花押，圆圈画成瓜子模样。举人老爷与把总为追赃还是示众呕气。阿Q被穿白背心、反缚双手，抬上无篷车游街。他在人群中发见吴妈，喊出半句“过了二十年又是一个……”，看客发出豺狼嗥叫般喝采。他想起饿狼眼睛，觉得灵魂被咬，未喊救命便仿佛微尘迸散而死。举人老爷因终未追赃全家号咷，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生上城报官被革命党翦了辫子，城里舆论不满枪毙不如杀头好看。

records.tagline: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明

records.tagline: 进秀才的赵家子，被问及阿Q名字
records.bio: 茂才先生是赵太爷的儿子，进过秀才，人称秀才、茂才先生、茂才公。他性格倨傲，对阿Q不屑一顾。阿Q酒后自称与赵太爷是本家，比秀才长三辈，叙述者问茂才先生阿Q名字写法，对方茫然。他拿大竹杠打阿Q，骂他忘八蛋。赵太爷怯叫老Q，他直呼阿Q。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。他与洋鬼子到静修庵革命打老尼姑。未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先。他托假洋鬼子带信并介绍进自由党，假洋鬼子向他讨还四块洋钱，他得银桃子。他上城报官被革命党翦了辫子。目前处境是上城报官被翦辫子。

records.tagline: 进过洋学堂、到过东洋，有假辫子，打阿Q
records.bio: 钱太爷的大儿子，人称假洋鬼子、洋先生、洋鬼子、秃儿、钱洋鬼子，是钱府主人，进过洋学堂，到过东洋，腿直了，辫子不见，戴假辫子。他性格跋扈，对阿Q动辄打骂。阿Q骂他秃儿驴，被他用哭丧棒打头，阿Q挨打后指认近旁孩子，又连挨几下。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。他与秀才到静修庵革命打老尼姑。赵秀才托他带信并介绍进自由党，他向秀才讨还四块洋钱，秀才得银桃子。阿Q去钱府找他想投革命，被他喝令滚出去。阿Q回土谷祠痛恨他，想告状害他。目前是革命党，母亲哭十几场，老婆跳三回井。

records.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
records.bio: 赵太爷是未庄有权势者，赵家主人。他性格专横，看不起阿Q。阿Q酒后自称与赵太爷是本家，比秀才长三辈，地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名。阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。举人老爷的船夜到赵府河埠头。邹七嫂说箱是破衣箱已被赵太爷回复。赵太爷怯叫老Q，秀才直呼阿Q。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。目前因儿子挂银桃子而骤然大阔，目空一切。

records.tagline: 百里闻名者，传言逃难寄箱
records.bio: 举人老爷是百里闻名者，帮办民政。他因革命党而逃难，将箱子寄到赵府。他与把总为追赃还是示众呕气。因终未追赃，举人老爷全家号咷。目前处境是全家号咷。

records.tagline: 赵家真正本家
records.bio: 赵白眼是赵家真正本家。赵白眼探阿Q口风，阿Q说其比己有钱。赵白眼回家把搭连交女人藏箱底。未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先。目前处境是买阿Q搭连，回家交女人藏箱底。

records.tagline: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，抢了阿Q的活
records.bio: 小D，又称小Don，是又瘦又乏的穷小子。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗。阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。阿Q见小D也盘辫，怒目而视吐唾沫。夜里阿Q遇小D，得知赵家遭抢。目前是阿Q的对手。

records.tagline: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
records.bio: 小尼姑是静修庵里的尼姑，新剃的头皮。阿Q迎上小尼姑吐唾沫并骂她，伸手摩小尼姑新剃的头皮并调笑，扭住小尼姑面颊并用力一拧，小尼姑带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。阿Q到静修庵问革命，老尼姑关门。秀才与洋鬼子到静修庵革命打老尼姑。目前处境是被秀才和洋鬼子打，龙牌碎，宣德𬬻不见。

records.tagline: 赵家真正本家
records.bio: 赵司晨是赵家真正本家。未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先。阿Q见赵司晨盘辫被称革命党，也学样盘辫。目前是阿Q同乡。

records.tagline: 坐堂审问阿Q的官员
records.bio: 老头子，满面剃得精光，是坐堂审问的官。阿Q上大堂见光头老头子，身不由己跪下，长衫人物吆喝阿Q站着不要跪，斥其奴隶性。老头子审问同党下落，阿Q答不知。目前是审问阿Q的官员。

records.text:
未庄有个叫阿Q的人，姓名籍贯都无从查考，叙述者只好为他写下这篇“正传”。阿Q酒后自称与赵太爷是本家，比秀才长三辈，结果被赵太爷叫去喝骂，打了他嘴巴，斥他不配姓赵，地保还索了二百文酒钱。阿Q与人吵架，总说先前比对方阔得多；被闲人取笑癞疮疤、揪住黄辫子碰响头，他自认虫豸，反以“第一个能自轻自贱”而心满意足。赌摊打架丢了洋钱，他便自打嘴巴，转败为胜。被赵太爷打后，他又自认是赵太爷的父亲而得意。与王胡捉虱子，因捉得少而骂人，被王胡撞墙五下，受了生平第一件屈辱；骂钱太爷的大儿子，又被哭丧棒打头。他调笑小尼姑，拧她面颊，酒店里的人大笑，他更加得意。

因小尼姑之事，阿Q夜里想起该有个女人。他在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，吴妈大叫跑出，秀才拿大竹杠打他，赵太爷也举竹杠奔来，阿Q逃走。地保来教训他，定下五条件并索酒钱，阿Q质了棉被，赤膊磕头。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不再赊欠，管祠老头子催他走。多日无人叫工，他打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗。阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，互拔辫子，相持半点钟后同时放手退开。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，被老尼姑斥偷，又被黑狗追咬，滚出墙外，吃完三个萝卜，打定进城的主意。

举人老爷的船夜到赵府，阿Q听说举人老爷怕革命党而神往，醉后大喊造反了。赵太爷怯叫老Q，秀才直呼阿Q。赵白眼探口风，阿Q说其比己有钱，赵白眼回家把搭连交女人藏箱底。管祠老头子请阿Q喝茶，阿Q要饼和烛，幻想革命党叫他同去，梦中排序该杀之人，包括小D、赵太爷、秀才、钱太爷的大儿子、王胡。秀才与洋鬼子到静修庵革命打老尼姑，阿Q去问革命，老尼姑关门。革命党进城后无大异样，未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先，赵司晨、赵白眼、阿Q也相继效仿。阿Q见小D也盘辫，怒目而视吐唾沫。赵秀才托假洋鬼子带信并介绍进自由党，假洋鬼子讨还四块洋钱，秀才得银桃子。阿Q去钱府想投革命，被假洋鬼子喝令滚出去，忧愁前程被一笔勾销。夜里阿Q遇小D，得知赵家遭抢，暗中看见白盔白甲的人搬走赵家箱笼器具，回土谷祠痛恨假洋鬼子，想告状害他。

赵家遭抢四天后，阿Q半夜被兵警抓进县城，关进栅栏小屋。他上大堂见光头老头子，身不由己跪下，供称“因为我想造反”，又答不知同党下落。被令画花押，圆圈画成瓜子模样。举人老爷与把总为追赃还是示众呕气。阿Q被穿白背心、反缚双手，抬上无篷车游街。他在人群中发见吴妈，喊出半句“过了二十年又是一个……”，看客发出豺狼嗥叫般喝采。他想起饿狼眼睛，觉得灵魂被咬，未喊救命便仿佛微尘迸散而死。举人老爷因终未追赃全家号咷，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生上城报官被革命党翦了辫子，城里舆论不满枪毙不如杀头好看。

$tuple.tagline: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
$tuple.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

$tuple.tagline: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
$tuple.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

$tuple.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
$tuple.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

$tuple.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
$tuple.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

$tuple.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
$tuple.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

$tuple.tagline: 又癞又胡的未庄人，扭打阿Q使其受辱
$tuple.bio: 未庄人，又癞又胡，人称王癞胡。他与阿Q本无深交，却因捉虱子一事结怨。阿Q与他并排坐下捉虱子，阿Q捉的虱子不如他多，心中不平，骂他毛虫，他回骂癞皮狗，并抓住阿Q辫子撞墙五下，使阿Q受生平第一件屈辱。目前他仍在未庄。

$tuple.tagline: 进秀才的赵家子，被问及阿Q名字
$tuple.bio: 赵太爷之子，进过秀才，人称茂才先生。他出身赵家，对阿Q一类人物并不放在眼里。叙述者曾问他阿Q名字的写法，他茫然不知。阿Q在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉时，他拿大竹杠打阿Q，骂他忘八蛋。目前他仍是赵家的秀才。

$tuple.tagline: 未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人
$tuple.bio: 未庄的闲人们，常以戏弄阿Q为乐。他们拿阿Q的癞疮疤取笑，喊“亮起来了”；揪住阿Q的黄辫子碰响头后得胜而去；又逼阿Q自认人打畜生，阿Q自认虫豸。目前他们仍是未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人。

$tuple.tagline: 赵太爷家唯一女仆，被阿Q调戏
$tuple.bio: 赵太爷家唯一的女仆，是个小孤孀，与邻居邹七嫂相熟。她本分守己，却因阿Q的举动受惊。阿Q在赵家厨房向她下跪求困觉，她楞了一息，发抖大叫着往外跑；少奶奶拖她出下房，邹七嫂劝她不要寻短见。目前她仍在赵太爷家做女仆。

$tuple.tagline: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，抢了阿Q的活
$tuple.bio: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，人称小Don。他本是无名之辈，却因谋了阿Q的饭碗而与阿Q结仇。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗；阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。目前他仍在未庄做短工。

$tuple.text: 赵家遭抢四天后，阿Q半夜被兵警抓进县城，关进栅栏小屋。他上大堂见光头老头子，身不由己跪下，供称“因为我想造反”，又答不知同党下落。被令画花押，圆圈画成瓜子模样。举人老爷与把总为追赃还是示众呕气。阿Q被穿白背心、反缚双手，抬上无篷车游街。他在人群中发见吴妈，喊出半句“过了二十年又是一个……”，看客发出豺狼嗥叫般喝采。他想起饿狼眼睛，觉得灵魂被咬，未喊救命便仿佛微尘迸散而死。举人老爷因终未追赃全家号咷，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生上城报官被革命党翦了辫子，城里舆论不满枪毙不如杀头好看。

$tuple.tagline: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明

$tuple.tagline: 进秀才的赵家子，被问及阿Q名字
$tuple.bio: 茂才先生是赵太爷的儿子，进过秀才，人称秀才、茂才先生、茂才公。他性格倨傲，对阿Q不屑一顾。阿Q酒后自称与赵太爷是本家，比秀才长三辈，叙述者问茂才先生阿Q名字写法，对方茫然。他拿大竹杠打阿Q，骂他忘八蛋。赵太爷怯叫老Q，他直呼阿Q。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。他与洋鬼子到静修庵革命打老尼姑。未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先。他托假洋鬼子带信并介绍进自由党，假洋鬼子向他讨还四块洋钱，他得银桃子。他上城报官被革命党翦了辫子。目前处境是上城报官被翦辫子。

$tuple.tagline: 进过洋学堂、到过东洋，有假辫子，打阿Q
$tuple.bio: 钱太爷的大儿子，人称假洋鬼子、洋先生、洋鬼子、秃儿、钱洋鬼子，是钱府主人，进过洋学堂，到过东洋，腿直了，辫子不见，戴假辫子。他性格跋扈，对阿Q动辄打骂。阿Q骂他秃儿驴，被他用哭丧棒打头，阿Q挨打后指认近旁孩子，又连挨几下。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。他与秀才到静修庵革命打老尼姑。赵秀才托他带信并介绍进自由党，他向秀才讨还四块洋钱，秀才得银桃子。阿Q去钱府找他想投革命，被他喝令滚出去。阿Q回土谷祠痛恨他，想告状害他。目前是革命党，母亲哭十几场，老婆跳三回井。

$tuple.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
$tuple.bio: 赵太爷是未庄有权势者，赵家主人。他性格专横，看不起阿Q。阿Q酒后自称与赵太爷是本家，比秀才长三辈，地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名。阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。举人老爷的船夜到赵府河埠头。邹七嫂说箱是破衣箱已被赵太爷回复。赵太爷怯叫老Q，秀才直呼阿Q。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。目前因儿子挂银桃子而骤然大阔，目空一切。

$tuple.tagline: 百里闻名者，传言逃难寄箱
$tuple.bio: 举人老爷是百里闻名者，帮办民政。他因革命党而逃难，将箱子寄到赵府。他与把总为追赃还是示众呕气。因终未追赃，举人老爷全家号咷。目前处境是全家号咷。

$tuple.tagline: 赵家真正本家
$tuple.bio: 赵白眼是赵家真正本家。赵白眼探阿Q口风，阿Q说其比己有钱。赵白眼回家把搭连交女人藏箱底。未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先。目前处境是买阿Q搭连，回家交女人藏箱底。

$tuple.tagline: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，抢了阿Q的活
$tuple.bio: 小D，又称小Don，是又瘦又乏的穷小子。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗。阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。阿Q见小D也盘辫，怒目而视吐唾沫。夜里阿Q遇小D，得知赵家遭抢。目前是阿Q的对手。

$tuple.tagline: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
$tuple.bio: 小尼姑是静修庵里的尼姑，新剃的头皮。阿Q迎上小尼姑吐唾沫并骂她，伸手摩小尼姑新剃的头皮并调笑，扭住小尼姑面颊并用力一拧，小尼姑带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。阿Q到静修庵问革命，老尼姑关门。秀才与洋鬼子到静修庵革命打老尼姑。目前处境是被秀才和洋鬼子打，龙牌碎，宣德𬬻不见。

$tuple.tagline: 赵家真正本家
$tuple.bio: 赵司晨是赵家真正本家。未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先。阿Q见赵司晨盘辫被称革命党，也学样盘辫。目前是阿Q同乡。

$tuple.tagline: 坐堂审问阿Q的官员
$tuple.bio: 老头子，满面剃得精光，是坐堂审问的官。阿Q上大堂见光头老头子，身不由己跪下，长衫人物吆喝阿Q站着不要跪，斥其奴隶性。老头子审问同党下落，阿Q答不知。目前是审问阿Q的官员。

$tuple.text:
未庄有个叫阿Q的人，姓名籍贯都无从查考，叙述者只好为他写下这篇“正传”。阿Q酒后自称与赵太爷是本家，比秀才长三辈，结果被赵太爷叫去喝骂，打了他嘴巴，斥他不配姓赵，地保还索了二百文酒钱。阿Q与人吵架，总说先前比对方阔得多；被闲人取笑癞疮疤、揪住黄辫子碰响头，他自认虫豸，反以“第一个能自轻自贱”而心满意足。赌摊打架丢了洋钱，他便自打嘴巴，转败为胜。被赵太爷打后，他又自认是赵太爷的父亲而得意。与王胡捉虱子，因捉得少而骂人，被王胡撞墙五下，受了生平第一件屈辱；骂钱太爷的大儿子，又被哭丧棒打头。他调笑小尼姑，拧她面颊，酒店里的人大笑，他更加得意。

因小尼姑之事，阿Q夜里想起该有个女人。他在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，吴妈大叫跑出，秀才拿大竹杠打他，赵太爷也举竹杠奔来，阿Q逃走。地保来教训他，定下五条件并索酒钱，阿Q质了棉被，赤膊磕头。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不再赊欠，管祠老头子催他走。多日无人叫工，他打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗。阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，互拔辫子，相持半点钟后同时放手退开。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，被老尼姑斥偷，又被黑狗追咬，滚出墙外，吃完三个萝卜，打定进城的主意。

举人老爷的船夜到赵府，阿Q听说举人老爷怕革命党而神往，醉后大喊造反了。赵太爷怯叫老Q，秀才直呼阿Q。赵白眼探口风，阿Q说其比己有钱，赵白眼回家把搭连交女人藏箱底。管祠老头子请阿Q喝茶，阿Q要饼和烛，幻想革命党叫他同去，梦中排序该杀之人，包括小D、赵太爷、秀才、钱太爷的大儿子、王胡。秀才与洋鬼子到静修庵革命打老尼姑，阿Q去问革命，老尼姑关门。革命党进城后无大异样，未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先，赵司晨、赵白眼、阿Q也相继效仿。阿Q见小D也盘辫，怒目而视吐唾沫。赵秀才托假洋鬼子带信并介绍进自由党，假洋鬼子讨还四块洋钱，秀才得银桃子。阿Q去钱府想投革命，被假洋鬼子喝令滚出去，忧愁前程被一笔勾销。夜里阿Q遇小D，得知赵家遭抢，暗中看见白盔白甲的人搬走赵家箱笼器具，回土谷祠痛恨假洋鬼子，想告状害他。

赵家遭抢四天后，阿Q半夜被兵警抓进县城，关进栅栏小屋。他上大堂见光头老头子，身不由己跪下，供称“因为我想造反”，又答不知同党下落。被令画花押，圆圈画成瓜子模样。举人老爷与把总为追赃还是示众呕气。阿Q被穿白背心、反缚双手，抬上无篷车游街。他在人群中发见吴妈，喊出半句“过了二十年又是一个……”，看客发出豺狼嗥叫般喝采。他想起饿狼眼睛，觉得灵魂被咬，未喊救命便仿佛微尘迸散而死。举人老爷因终未追赃全家号咷，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生上城报官被革命党翦了辫子，城里舆论不满枪毙不如杀头好看。

records.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
records.bio: Mr. Utterson is a lawyer and the distant kinsman and friend of Mr. Richard Enfield. He is austere, tolerant, and undemonstrative, and is known as the last good influence on downgoing men. On a Sunday walk with Enfield, he was shown a sinister door and heard Enfield's account of a man who trampled a girl and paid with a cheque. Utterson asked whether the cheque drawer lived there, asked the man's name, and asked whether Hyde used a key. He said he already knew the other party's name. He and Enfield agreed never to refer to the matter again. He remains a lawyer and the last good influence on downgoing men.

records.tagline: Utterson's distant kinsman, man about town
records.bio: Mr. Richard Enfield is Utterson's distant kinsman and a man about town. He dislikes asking questions and calls it delicacy. On a Sunday walk with Utterson, he pointed his cane at a sinister door and said it was connected with a very odd story. He collared a man who had trampled a girl, forced him to pay a hundred pounds, and spent the night with him in his chambers before taking him to the bank, where the cheque proved genuine. He called the door place Black Mail House, described the door house, named the man as Hyde, and confirmed Hyde still has the key and used it a week ago. He agreed with Utterson never to refer to the matter again.

records.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
records.bio: The man in the middle, later named Hyde, is a person of extraordinary appearance who gives a feeling of deformity. He is cool, sneering, and Satan-like. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, then was collared by Enfield and brought back to the group around the child. The doctor turned sick and white with desire to kill him. Threatened with scandal, he was forced to pay a hundred pounds. He led them to the door, unlocked it, and returned with gold and a cheque, offering to stay until the banks opened and cash it himself. They spent the night in Enfield's chambers and went to the bank next day. He still has a key and used it a week ago.

records.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
records.bio: Edward Hyde is a small, plainly dressed man with a husky, whispering, broken voice, known as Jekyll's friend and benefactor, living in Soho. He is merciless and inspires enduring hatred. He trampled a girl and paid a hundred pounds with a cheque from Jekyll's account. Jekyll's will names him heir if Jekyll vanishes. Utterson accosted him at the by-street door; Hyde gave his Soho address, accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll, then unlocked the door and disappeared. records.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor

He is hearty, red-faced, prematurely white-haired, boisterous, decided, theatrical but genuine. Utterson came to consult him about Jekyll's will and Hyde. Lanyon welcomed him warmly, said Jekyll had become too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago, and had never heard of Hyde. He now remains Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor, unaware of Hyde's identity.

records.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
records.bio: Poole is the elderly servant and butler at Dr. Jekyll's house, serving his master Dr. Jekyll and obeying the man in the middle as an obeyed superior. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's house and told him Jekyll had gone out. He confirmed that Hyde has a key and comes by the dissecting room door, that all servants have orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dines there and mostly uses the laboratory. He now continues in his post, bound by orders to obey Hyde.

records.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
records.bio: Dr. Henry Jekyll, M.D., D.C.L., L.L.D., F.R.S., is a doctor, old friend of Mr. Utterson and Dr. Lanyon, and master of Poole. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. Lanyon said Jekyll became too fanciful and wrong in mind over ten years ago. Utterson asked Lanyon whether they were Jekyll's two oldest friends. Jekyll is now from home, gone out, while his servants are ordered to obey Hyde.

records.bio: G. J. Utterson is a lawyer, a kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and an old friend of both Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past who is troubled by old sins. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

records.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
records.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

records.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
records.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

records.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
records.bio: Poole is the elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house, obedient to his master and to Hyde as his superior. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. Utterson now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering, and Poole reports that Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

records.tagline: Utterson's head clerk and handwriting expert
records.bio: Mr. Guest is Utterson's head clerk and a critic of handwriting. Utterson showed him the murderer's autograph letter, and Guest compared it with Jekyll's note and found the two identical. That is all that is known of him to this point; he remains in Utterson's employ.

records.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
records.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

$tuple.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
$tuple.bio: G. J. Utterson is a lawyer, a kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and an old friend of both Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past who is troubled by old sins. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

$tuple.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
$tuple.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

$tuple.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
$tuple.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

$tuple.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
$tuple.bio: Poole is the elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house, obedient to his master and to Hyde as his superior. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. Utterson now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering, and Poole reports that Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

$tuple.tagline: Utterson's head clerk and handwriting expert
$tuple.bio: Mr. Guest is Utterson's head clerk and a critic of handwriting. Utterson showed him the murderer's autograph letter, and Guest compared it with Jekyll's note and found the two identical. That is all that is known of him to this point; he remains in Utterson's employ.

$tuple.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

records.tagline: Lawyer, kinsman and friend of Enfield
records.bio: G. J. Utterson is a lawyer, a kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and an old friend of both Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past who is troubled by old sins. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

records.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
records.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

records.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
records.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

records.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
records.bio: Poole is the elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house, obedient to his master and to Hyde as his superior. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. Utterson now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering, and Poole reports that Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

records.tagline: Utterson's head clerk and handwriting expert
records.bio: Mr. Guest is Utterson's head clerk and a critic of handwriting. Utterson showed him the murderer's autograph letter, and Guest compared it with Jekyll's note and found the two identical. That is all that is known of him to this point; he remains in Utterson's employ.

records.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
records.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

$tuple.bio: G. J. Utterson is a lawyer, a kinsman and friend of Richard Enfield, and an old friend of both Dr. Jekyll and Dr. Lanyon. He is a man of blameless past who is troubled by old sins. After Enfield told him of a faceless figure at a by-street door, he lay awake haunted, kept watch by that door, and resolved to hunt for Hyde. He accosted Hyde, studied his face, and was deeply disturbed. He raised Jekyll's will, promised to bear with Hyde, identified Sir Danvers Carew's body, recognized his own stick as the weapon, searched Hyde's rooms, and heard Guest find Hyde's letter identical with Jekyll's hand. He dined with Jekyll and Lanyon, then found Jekyll shut against him and Lanyon refusing Jekyll's name. After Lanyon's funeral he opened the sealed envelope, whose enclosure must wait for Jekyll's death or disappearance. He now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering.

$tuple.tagline: Doctor whose will names Hyde as heir
$tuple.bio: Henry Jekyll is a doctor, connoisseur and old friend of Utterson and Lanyon, known for charities and religion. He is fifty, large, well-made and smooth-faced, with a slyish cast. Over ten years ago Lanyon found him too fanciful and wrong in mind. His will leaves all his possessions to Edward Hyde, who inherits if Jekyll vanishes. When Utterson raised the will and Hyde, Jekyll paled, refused to hear more, called Lanyon a hide-bound pedant, said he could be rid of Hyde whenever he chose, and asked Utterson to help Hyde for his sake. He swore he would never set eyes on Hyde again, gave Utterson Hyde's letter to judge, admitted Hyde dictated the will, then emerged and resumed old friendships. He later shut his door against Utterson, wrote of an incurable quarrel, vowed extreme seclusion and an unnameable punishment. He now confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

$tuple.tagline: Utterson's old friend and fellow doctor
$tuple.bio: Dr. Lanyon is a doctor with a house in Cavendish Square, an old friend of Utterson and formerly of Dr. Jekyll. He is boisterous, decided and theatrical but genuine. Over ten years ago he judged Jekyll too fanciful and wrong in mind. When Utterson asked about Hyde, Lanyon had never heard of him. He dined with Jekyll and Utterson as inseparable friends, but later Utterson found him visibly decayed; Lanyon declared himself a doomed man who would never recover, refused to hear Jekyll's name and called him dead to him. He took to his bed and died within a fortnight. After his funeral Utterson opened the sealed envelope Lanyon left, whose enclosure is not to be opened till Jekyll's death or disappearance. He is dead.

$tuple.tagline: Elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house
$tuple.bio: Poole is the elderly servant at Dr. Jekyll's house, obedient to his master and to Hyde as his superior. He told Utterson that Jekyll had gone out, confirmed Hyde had a key and came by the dissecting room door, said all servants had orders to obey Hyde, and that Hyde never dined there and mostly used the laboratory. He admitted Utterson to Jekyll's cabinet and told him no letter came except by post. He reported that Jekyll had shut his door against Utterson and was confined. Utterson now prefers speaking with Poole at the door rather than entering, and Poole reports that Jekyll confines himself over the laboratory and is silent.

$tuple.tagline: Utterson's head clerk and handwriting expert
$tuple.bio: Mr. Guest is Utterson's head clerk and a critic of handwriting. Utterson showed him the murderer's autograph letter, and Guest compared it with Jekyll's note and found the two identical. That is all that is known of him to this point; he remains in Utterson's employ.

$tuple.tagline: Tramples a girl, pays with a cheque
$tuple.bio: Edward Hyde is a young man in whom Dr. Jekyll takes great interest, the favourite of Jekyll, and the heir named in Jekyll's will. He is merciless, inspires enduring hatred, and impresses beholders with a sense of unexpressed deformity. He trampled over a girl's body and left her screaming, was forced by threats of scandal to pay a hundred pounds, and led Enfield's group to a door where he returned with gold and a cheque. He later met Utterson at that door, gave his address in Soho, angrily accused Utterson of lying about Jekyll's description, and disappeared into the house. The maid saw him beat Sir Danvers Carew to death with a cane. He had few familiars, no traceable family, no photograph, and several thousand pounds to his credit. He has vanished from police knowledge; rewards are offered.

records.text: 阿Q回土谷祠后省悟古怪在于自己赤膊，未庄女人见他便躲，邹七嫂也叫女儿进去。酒店不再赊欠，管祠老头子催他走。多日无人叫工，他饿着打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗。阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，相持半点钟后同时放手退开。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，决计出门求食，翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，小尼姑探头又缩回，老尼姑出来斥他偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑，被黑狗追咬，爬上桑树滚出墙外。吃完三个萝卜，他打定进城的主意。

records.tagline: 被立传的未庄人，姓氏籍贯不明
records.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

records.tagline: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
records.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

records.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
records.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

records.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
records.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

records.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
records.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

records.tagline: 又癞又胡的未庄人，扭打阿Q使其受辱
records.bio: 未庄人，又癞又胡，人称王癞胡。他与阿Q本无深交，却因捉虱子一事结怨。阿Q与他并排坐下捉虱子，阿Q捉的虱子不如他多，心中不平，骂他毛虫，他回骂癞皮狗，并抓住阿Q辫子撞墙五下，使阿Q受生平第一件屈辱。目前他仍在未庄。

records.tagline: 进秀才的赵家子，被问及阿Q名字
records.bio: 赵太爷之子，进过秀才，人称茂才先生。他出身赵家，对阿Q一类人物并不放在眼里。叙述者曾问他阿Q名字的写法，他茫然不知。阿Q在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉时，他拿大竹杠打阿Q，骂他忘八蛋。目前他仍是赵家的秀才。

records.tagline: 未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人
records.bio: 未庄的闲人们，常以戏弄阿Q为乐。他们拿阿Q的癞疮疤取笑，喊“亮起来了”；揪住阿Q的黄辫子碰响头后得胜而去；又逼阿Q自认人打畜生，阿Q自认虫豸。目前他们仍是未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人。

records.tagline: 赵太爷家唯一女仆，被阿Q调戏
records.bio: 赵太爷家唯一的女仆，是个小孤孀，与邻居邹七嫂相熟。她本分守己，却因阿Q的举动受惊。阿Q在赵家厨房向她下跪求困觉，她楞了一息，发抖大叫着往外跑；少奶奶拖她出下房，邹七嫂劝她不要寻短见。目前她仍在赵太爷家做女仆。

records.tagline: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，抢了阿Q的活
records.bio: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，人称小Don。他本是无名之辈，却因谋了阿Q的饭碗而与阿Q结仇。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗；阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。目前他仍在未庄做短工。

records.bio: 茂才先生是赵太爷的儿子，进过秀才，人称秀才、茂才先生、茂才公。他性格倨傲，对阿Q不屑一顾。阿Q酒后自称与赵太爷是本家，比秀才长三辈，叙述者问茂才先生阿Q名字写法，对方茫然。他拿大竹杠打阿Q，骂他忘八蛋。赵太爷怯叫老Q，他直呼阿Q。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。他与洋鬼子到静修庵革命打老尼姑。未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先。他托假洋鬼子带信并介绍进自由党，假洋鬼子向他讨还四块洋钱，他得银桃子。他上城报官被革命党翦了辫子。目前处境是上城报官被翦辫子。

records.tagline: 进过洋学堂、到过东洋，有假辫子，打阿Q
records.bio: 钱太爷的大儿子，人称假洋鬼子、洋先生、洋鬼子、秃儿、钱洋鬼子，是钱府主人，进过洋学堂，到过东洋，腿直了，辫子不见，戴假辫子。他性格跋扈，对阿Q动辄打骂。阿Q骂他秃儿驴，被他用哭丧棒打头，阿Q挨打后指认近旁孩子，又连挨几下。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。他与秀才到静修庵革命打老尼姑。赵秀才托他带信并介绍进自由党，他向秀才讨还四块洋钱，秀才得银桃子。阿Q去钱府找他想投革命，被他喝令滚出去。阿Q回土谷祠痛恨他，想告状害他。目前是革命党，母亲哭十几场，老婆跳三回井。

records.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
records.bio: 赵太爷是未庄有权势者，赵家主人。他性格专横，看不起阿Q。阿Q酒后自称与赵太爷是本家，比秀才长三辈，地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名。阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。举人老爷的船夜到赵府河埠头。邹七嫂说箱是破衣箱已被赵太爷回复。赵太爷怯叫老Q，秀才直呼阿Q。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。目前因儿子挂银桃子而骤然大阔，目空一切。

records.tagline: 百里闻名者，传言逃难寄箱
records.bio: 举人老爷是百里闻名者，帮办民政。他因革命党而逃难，将箱子寄到赵府。他与把总为追赃还是示众呕气。因终未追赃，举人老爷全家号咷。目前处境是全家号咷。

records.tagline: 赵家真正本家
records.bio: 赵白眼是赵家真正本家。赵白眼探阿Q口风，阿Q说其比己有钱。赵白眼回家把搭连交女人藏箱底。未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先。目前处境是买阿Q搭连，回家交女人藏箱底。

records.tagline: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，抢了阿Q的活
records.bio: 小D，又称小Don，是又瘦又乏的穷小子。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗。阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。阿Q见小D也盘辫，怒目而视吐唾沫。夜里阿Q遇小D，得知赵家遭抢。目前是阿Q的对手。

records.tagline: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
records.bio: 小尼姑是静修庵里的尼姑，新剃的头皮。阿Q迎上小尼姑吐唾沫并骂她，伸手摩小尼姑新剃的头皮并调笑，扭住小尼姑面颊并用力一拧，小尼姑带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。阿Q到静修庵问革命，老尼姑关门。秀才与洋鬼子到静修庵革命打老尼姑。目前处境是被秀才和洋鬼子打，龙牌碎，宣德𬬻不见。

records.tagline: 赵家真正本家
records.bio: 赵司晨是赵家真正本家。未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先。阿Q见赵司晨盘辫被称革命党，也学样盘辫。目前是阿Q同乡。

records.tagline: 坐堂审问阿Q的官员
records.bio: 老头子，满面剃得精光，是坐堂审问的官。阿Q上大堂见光头老头子，身不由己跪下，长衫人物吆喝阿Q站着不要跪，斥其奴隶性。老头子审问同党下落，阿Q答不知。目前是审问阿Q的官员。

$tuple.bio: 未庄的短工，姓氏籍贯不明，人称阿Quei，住在土谷祠。他自尊自负，又惯于自轻自贱，常以精神胜利法自解。因自称与赵太爷是本家，被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名；后与王胡捉虱子起争执，被撞墙五下，受生平第一件屈辱；又骂假洋鬼子，被哭丧棒打头；调戏小尼姑后，在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉，被秀才用大竹杠打出，地保定下五条件并索酒钱，他质了棉被履行条约。此后未庄女人见他便躲，酒店不赊欠，无人叫他做短工，小D又谋了他的饭碗。他卖尽棉被毡帽布衫棉袄，翻墙进静修庵偷萝卜，被老尼姑斥骂、黑狗追咬，吃完三个萝卜后打定进城的主意。

$tuple.tagline: 静修庵的尼姑，被阿Q调戏
$tuple.bio: 静修庵里的尼姑，新剃了头皮。她与阿Q本无往来，却因阿Q的调笑而受辱。阿Q迎上她吐唾沫并骂她，又伸手摩她新剃的头皮并调笑，还扭住她的面颊用力一拧，她带哭地骂阿Q断子绝孙。后来阿Q翻墙进静修庵菜园拔萝卜，她的圆头从门口伸出又缩回，随后老尼姑出来斥阿Q偷萝卜，阿Q抵赖后拔步便跑。目前她仍在静修庵中。

$tuple.tagline: 为阿Q作传的叙述者
$tuple.bio: 为阿Q作传的叙述者，决意给阿Q作正传，已想了一两年。他为文章名目犯难，最终取“正传”二字；曾问赵太爷的儿子茂才先生阿Q名字的写法，对方茫然；又托同乡查案卷，无果，遂写作阿Q。他不知阿Q的籍贯，只知其多住未庄。目前他仍在为阿Q立传。

$tuple.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
$tuple.bio: 未庄有权势者，赵家主人，赵太爷的儿子茂才先生之父。他威势十足，不容冒犯。阿Q酒后自称与他是本家、比秀才长三辈，他叫地保传阿Q来，喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被他打嘴巴而出了名。后来阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。目前他仍是未庄有权势的赵家主人。

$tuple.tagline: 传唤并训斥阿Q的村中差役
$tuple.bio: 村中地保，传唤训斥阿Q，是赵太爷的下属。他惯于仗势训人、索要酒钱。地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打阿Q嘴巴，他与阿Q退出后训斥阿Q并谢二百文酒钱；阿Q付给他二百文酒钱后忿忿躺下。后来阿Q调戏吴妈事发，地保来教训阿Q，定下五条件并索酒钱。目前他仍是村中地保。

$tuple.tagline: 又癞又胡的未庄人，扭打阿Q使其受辱
$tuple.bio: 未庄人，又癞又胡，人称王癞胡。他与阿Q本无深交，却因捉虱子一事结怨。阿Q与他并排坐下捉虱子，阿Q捉的虱子不如他多，心中不平，骂他毛虫，他回骂癞皮狗，并抓住阿Q辫子撞墙五下，使阿Q受生平第一件屈辱。目前他仍在未庄。

$tuple.tagline: 进秀才的赵家子，被问及阿Q名字
$tuple.bio: 赵太爷之子，进过秀才，人称茂才先生。他出身赵家，对阿Q一类人物并不放在眼里。叙述者曾问他阿Q名字的写法，他茫然不知。阿Q在赵家厨房向吴妈下跪求困觉时，他拿大竹杠打阿Q，骂他忘八蛋。目前他仍是赵家的秀才。

$tuple.tagline: 未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人
$tuple.bio: 未庄的闲人们，常以戏弄阿Q为乐。他们拿阿Q的癞疮疤取笑，喊“亮起来了”；揪住阿Q的黄辫子碰响头后得胜而去；又逼阿Q自认人打畜生，阿Q自认虫豸。目前他们仍是未庄中戏弄阿Q的众人。

$tuple.tagline: 赵太爷家唯一女仆，被阿Q调戏
$tuple.bio: 赵太爷家唯一的女仆，是个小孤孀，与邻居邹七嫂相熟。她本分守己，却因阿Q的举动受惊。阿Q在赵家厨房向她下跪求困觉，她楞了一息，发抖大叫着往外跑；少奶奶拖她出下房，邹七嫂劝她不要寻短见。目前她仍在赵太爷家做女仆。

$tuple.tagline: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，抢了阿Q的活
$tuple.bio: 又瘦又乏的穷小子，人称小Don。他本是无名之辈，却因谋了阿Q的饭碗而与阿Q结仇。阿Q打听出众人改叫小D，小D谋了他的饭碗；阿Q在钱府照壁前遇小D，扑上去互拔辫子，两人势均力敌相持半点钟，同时放手退开。目前他仍在未庄做短工。

$tuple.bio: 茂才先生是赵太爷的儿子，进过秀才，人称秀才、茂才先生、茂才公。他性格倨傲，对阿Q不屑一顾。阿Q酒后自称与赵太爷是本家，比秀才长三辈，叙述者问茂才先生阿Q名字写法，对方茫然。他拿大竹杠打阿Q，骂他忘八蛋。赵太爷怯叫老Q，他直呼阿Q。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。他与洋鬼子到静修庵革命打老尼姑。未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先。他托假洋鬼子带信并介绍进自由党，假洋鬼子向他讨还四块洋钱，他得银桃子。他上城报官被革命党翦了辫子。目前处境是上城报官被翦辫子。

$tuple.tagline: 进过洋学堂、到过东洋，有假辫子，打阿Q
$tuple.bio: 钱太爷的大儿子，人称假洋鬼子、洋先生、洋鬼子、秃儿、钱洋鬼子，是钱府主人，进过洋学堂，到过东洋，腿直了，辫子不见，戴假辫子。他性格跋扈，对阿Q动辄打骂。阿Q骂他秃儿驴，被他用哭丧棒打头，阿Q挨打后指认近旁孩子，又连挨几下。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。他与秀才到静修庵革命打老尼姑。赵秀才托他带信并介绍进自由党，他向秀才讨还四块洋钱，秀才得银桃子。阿Q去钱府找他想投革命，被他喝令滚出去。阿Q回土谷祠痛恨他，想告状害他。目前是革命党，母亲哭十几场，老婆跳三回井。

$tuple.tagline: 未庄有权势者，否认与阿Q同宗
$tuple.bio: 赵太爷是未庄有权势者，赵家主人。他性格专横，看不起阿Q。阿Q酒后自称与赵太爷是本家，比秀才长三辈，地保叫阿Q去赵家，赵太爷喝骂并打他嘴巴，斥阿Q不配姓赵，阿Q不抗辩。阿Q因被赵太爷打嘴巴而出了名。阿Q见赵太爷拿竹杠奔来，翻身逃走。举人老爷的船夜到赵府河埠头。邹七嫂说箱是破衣箱已被赵太爷回复。赵太爷怯叫老Q，秀才直呼阿Q。阿Q梦中排序该杀之人。目前因儿子挂银桃子而骤然大阔，目空一切。

$tuple.bio: 举人老爷是百里闻名者，帮办民政。他因革命党而逃难，将箱子寄到赵府。他与把总为追赃还是示众呕气。因终未追赃，举人老爷全家号咷。目前处境是全家号咷。

$tuple.bio: 赵白眼是赵家真正本家。赵白眼探阿Q口风，阿Q说其比己有钱。赵白眼回家把搭连交女人藏箱底。未庄人陆续将辫子盘在顶上，茂才公最先。目前处境是买阿Q搭连，回家交女人藏箱底。
